new_points.title: Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeats Texas governor Greg Abbott in stunning upset
new_points.content: Hinojosa wins momentous victory, shatters Republican grip on key office and will become state’s first Latina governorUS midterm elections – live updatesTrack live results from all 50 statesIn a stunning political upset that would have seemed improbable only a few weeks ago, Democrat Gina Hinojosa has defeated three-term governor Greg Abbott on Tuesday, shattering the Republican grip on the state’s highest and most powerful executive office.Hinojosa’s historic victory – she will be the state’s first ever Latina governor – ended Abbott’s bid for an unprecedented fourth term, and delivered Democrats their most consequential victory in the state in a generation.

new_points.title: Democrat Sherrod Brown wins Ohio Senate race in major blow to Republicans

new_points.title: Democrats on brink of retaking Senate from Republicans after series of historic wins

It was a stunning turnaround for the party, two years after voters put them into the minority in Congress’s upper chamber as they returned Trump to the White House.

new_points.title: Xavier Becerra wins California race for governor with vows to resist Trump’s agenda

Becerra was the overwhelming favorite to defeat Steve Hilton, the Republican endorsed by Trump.

new_points.title: Amy Acton wins Ohio race for governor, ending 16 years of Republican control of office

She will become the first woman to serve as Ohio’s governor. Her defeat of Vivek Ramaswamy, the biotech entrepreneur endorsed by Trump, also ends 16 years of Republican control of the governor’s office. She is the first Democrat to win the post since Ted Strickland in 2006.

new_points.title: Kids who eat more ultra-processed foods show a troubling brain response
new_points.content: A new study suggests that ultra-processed foods may influence children's developing brains in ways that encourage weight gain. Researchers from USC studied 46 children ages 7 to 10 and found that those who ate more ultra-processed foods showed stronger activity in the brain's reward system when viewing tempting foods like cookies and French fries. These heightened brain responses were linked to greater increases in body fat and body mass index (BMI) one year later, suggesting that the brain's sensitivity to food cues may help explain why ultra-processed diets are associated with obesity.
